The log requires exactly-once semantics at the protocol level, which is achieved by making the network request itself safe to retry (safe at the transport layer) while the payload carries an idempotency key (idempotent payload). Thus, the property required is a composite: safe transport, idempotent payload.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the system lacks an idempotency key but the writer is a pure function of state, a safe retry might still inject duplicates.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the transport layer provides exactly-once guarantees natively, the writers need neither to be safe nor idempotent in their payload.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"At-least-once delivery relies on retries. To make retries harmless, the transport operation must be safe. To make the log deterministic, the payload must carry an idempotency key so the log can collapse the retried safe operations into a single entry. Neither property alone is sufficient.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
